notes: Each state's 1985 and 1990 values are columns (dthrte85 and dthrte90 to speed85 and speed90), so the long form is state x year over four measures named by their columns' stem, state naming each wide row once; the package's code holds no reshape. The vignette's Example 13.7 fits lm(cdthrte ~ copen + cadmn), a first-difference model of the change in traffic deaths per 100 million miles on the changes in open-container and administrative-revocation laws, a model of the contrast between the years, filed here on the long form as a Gaussian GLMM with year as a covariate and a random intercept per state. The 50 states and DC are many units over two years, a panel. speed (a 65 mph limit, 0 in 1985) is unused; the change columns are derived, ignored.

formula: cbind(rtis, patients - rtis) ~ arm + (1 + arm | study)
notes: The help page's columns pair each study's treatment group (xt respiratory tract infections of nt patients) with its control group (xc of nc), so the long form is study x arm, the arms named as the page names the groups; the page calls no reshape. Its examples pool log odds ratios by rma.mh(measure = 'OR') and by rma(yi, vi, method = 'DL'), the random-effects model filed here at the arm level as a binomial GLMM with a random intercept and a random arm effect per study. year, conceal and blind are unused.

Ecdat help (terrorism): Global Terrorism Database incidents by location for 204 countries and each year 1970 to 2020; 1993's data were lost and the year is absent from the loaded table. Stack: incidents at each year column; the countries are row names, absent from the loaded table, so country numbers the wide rows. Ecdat's terrorism holds only world and US totals per year; no model, so crossed random intercepts of country and year are proposed. The counts are mostly zero and overdispersed.

The help page calls it a 'Wide dataset to be used for growth modeling': each student's reading scores in fall kindergarten, spring kindergarten and spring first grade as fall_k, spring_k and spring_g1, so the long form is student x wave, the measure named by the page's word and the occasions by the column names, the page giving no numeric times; studentid is unique per row. Neither the page nor MLMusingR's code reshapes or models it. The formula is the reader's: wave by intervention (int, treatment or control) means and female, with a random intercept per student; three occasions per student leave no room for a random wave effect. Two scores are missing, rows for the contract to drop.

Ecdat help (terrorism): Global Terrorism Database deaths by location for 204 countries and each year 1970 to 2020, deaths missing in GTD counted as 0; 1993's data were lost and the year is absent from the loaded table. Stack: deaths at each year column; the countries are row names, absent from the loaded table, so country numbers the wide rows. Ecdat's terrorism holds only world and US totals per year; no model, so crossed random intercepts of country and year are proposed. The counts are mostly zero and overdispersed.

Help page cohesion: five cohesion items (COH01 to COH05, 'First' to 'Fifth Cohesion Variable') from 11 individuals in four platoons nested within two units, a demonstration table of the package's 'Multilevel Modeling in R'. No individual id, so a new unit soldier numbers the wide rows; the stack makes soldier x item. The page and the package's tree fit no model; the ratings are the documented measurement, 1 to 5, ordinal as Likert ratings are filed. The formula is the reader's: item a design factor of the scale's five items, the platoon (PLATOON within UNIT, four in all, fewer than five) a design factor, soldier intercepts. One rating missing.

RESPONSE INFERRED: no labels and no do-file uses the table, so the stack is read off the column names: twin1 and twin2 are the two members' values (1 to 21) of a twin pair, dzmz the pair's zygosity (dz or mz) and num2 the pairs showing that pattern, a frequency weight (ignored, as twin_hay's freq), pair numbering the 267 patterns. twin1 is never below twin2, so the members are ordered by value and member, the occasion, is ignored. A weighted fit makes each of a pattern's num2 pairs a pair of its own (as twin_hay's pair). The random intercept per pair is a proposal; a twin model would let its variance differ by zygosity.

milk.Rd: each of 17 panelists assessed two milk samples for sweetness, one with four units of additive (four) and one with one unit (one). The example plots four ~ one, no model. The long form is panelist x additive, additive the units (4, 1); the model is proposed.

formula: cbind(exa, total - exa) ~ arm + (1 + arm | study)
notes: The help page's columns hold each study's tiotropium group (tiotropium.*) and control group (placebo.*): the patients in total and those with at least one exacerbation, severe exacerbation, hospitalization, death, serious adverse event and withdrawal, so the long form is study x arm, the measures named by the columns' stems and the arms by their prefixes, study unique per row; the page calls no reshape. Its examples compute log odds ratios of exacerbation by escalc(measure = 'OR', ai = tiotropium.exa, n1i = tiotropium.total, ci = placebo.exa, n2i = placebo.total) and the SGRQ mean differences by escalc(measure = 'MD'), and draw them by bayesmeta's forestplot; the page fits no model beyond the forest plots. The formula is the reader's arm-level rendering of a random-effects meta-analysis of the odds ratios, a binomial GLMM with a random intercept and arm effect per study. The other end points (Karner et al. 2014's further analyses) are alternate responses, and sgrq.md, sgrq.se, fev1.md and fev1.se study-level contrasts outside the stack, all ignored. year, duration, inhaler, the baseline.* covariates and the rob.* risk-of-bias ratings are unused.

formula: ftp ~ survey + race + sex + reason + (1 | person)
notes: Ecdat help: 452 people's first unemployment spell (Romeo 1999, semiparametric duration models): duration, spell completed, race, sex, reason, search and pubemp once per person, and ftp1 to ftp4 whether the person searched for full-time work at survey 1 to 4. Stack: ftp at survey 1 to 4; person numbers the wide rows. The documented model is the duration's, with the search indicators as covariates; the page fits none on the long form, so a person random intercept with survey, race, sex and reason is proposed; duration, spell and nobs (the spell's observations) belong to the duration model and are ignored. ftp is 0 or 1 at all four surveys, also past nobs, which the help leaves unexplained.

RAO.ASC: jaw bone length (mm) of 20 boys measured on four fixed occasions, at ages 8, 8.5, 9 and 9.5 years, citing Elston and Grizzle (1962); boy numbers the wide rows. The source states no model; its references (Goldstein 1986, 1987, 1989) fit growth curves to these data, so the linear growth model with a boy intercept is proposed.

formula: cbind(resp, n - resp) ~ 0 + factor(id) + treatment + (1 | id) + (1 | id:treatment)
notes: The help page's columns hold up to three arms per trial ('wide arm-based format'): arm k's treatment, patients and counts of early responders, early remissions, losses to follow-up, losses due to adverse events and patients with adverse events in treatmentk, nk, respk, remik, lossk, loss.aek and aek, so the long form is trial x arm, the measures named by the columns' stems and arm numbered 1 to 3 as the page numbers the arms, id unique per row; the 58 two-arm trials leave arm 3 empty (treatment blank, counts missing), rows for the contract to drop. Its examples turn the arms into log odds ratios by pairwise(treat = list(treatment1, treatment2, treatment3), event = list(resp1, resp2, resp3), n = list(n1, n2, n3), studlab = id, sm = 'OR') and fit the random-effects network meta-analysis netmeta(pw1, common = FALSE, reference = 'Placebo'), the primary outcome early response filed here. Rendered as dat.linde2016 is filed: the arm-based model with fixed study effects and compound-symmetric arm effects, (1 | id) + (1 | id:treatment) with equal variances, id:treatment one arm per row (no three-arm trial repeats a treatment); published_model no, since netmeta fits normal log odds ratios after pairwise(). remi (model 2), loss, loss.ae and ae are alternate responses, author a label and arm the arm's position; year is unused. dat.linde2016 holds the response counts of the same pharmacological trials (Lecrubier 1997 and Blashki 1971 match) among its 93, for the merge's copy check.

formula: typ ~ context * I(trial %in% c("kita", "tulver")) * teleo + (1 | trial) + (1 | ID)
notes: IsOughtFolkBiology_Study4_Results.Rmd gathers v_dist, v_typ and v_sample, their lorp, kita and tulver columns and the normative items into item by response, marks the trial (virdex, lorp, kita, tulver) by the item's prefix, the functional ideal teleo (left, right) by virdex_tel to tulver_tel, and time current for virdex and lorp, future for kita and tulver; the stack holds the three judgments and teleo. It fits result_typ = clmm(response ~ context + time + teleo + context:time + context:teleo + time:teleo + context:time:teleo + (1|trial) + (1|ID), link = 'logit', threshold = 'flexible'), filed here with time written as its recode of trial, so its terms stay in the formula only; sample selection and distribution follow as rows 2 and 3. The 32 normative items (norm, wrong, best and done of each kind's two features, e.g. v_norm_many_1) cross the feature with the trial, so they stay outside the stack (ignored as alternate responses). trial has four levels.

formula: crbsi ~ factor(study) + arm + (0 + I(as.numeric(arm == "anti-infective")) | study) + offset(log(days))
notes: The help page's columns pair each study's anti-infective catheter group (x1i CRBSIs over t1i catheter days) with its standard catheter group (x2i over t2i), so the long form is study x arm, the arms as the page names the catheters, study (study number) unique per row; the page calls no reshape. Its examples fit the inverse-variance random-effects rma(measure = 'IRR') and the random-effects conditional Poisson model rma.glmm(measure = 'IRR', model = 'CM.EL'), a GLMM of the arm counts (Stijnen et al. 2010), filed here: conditioning on each study's total events stands for fixed study effects, with a random treatment effect per study, written as factor(study) + arm and a random anti-infective indicator by study (as dat.tian2009 is filed), the catheter days an offset. authors is a label; year is unused.

Gilgai line transect in New South Wales (Webster 1977; Laslett 1989): soil sampled at depths 0-10, 30-40 and 80-90 cm at each sampling location of a linear grid 4 m apart, pH, electrical conductivity and chloride measured on each sample. The stack is location x depth, the depth by the top of its interval in cm, the three measures named by the page's quantities. MASS ships no example or script for the table, and its sources model the transect spatially (spectral analysis, kriging), so published_model is no and the formula is the reader's: depth with a location intercept, the spatial correlation along the transect left out. One row per measure in the page's order: conductivity and chloride are rows 2 and 3.

like counts how often monk A named monk B as liked over three rounds, a binomial out of a constant 3 that no column holds, so it is filed count (eggprod ruling). McElreath's Statistical Rethinking 2022 course (week 8, recalled, not in the cache; the help page lists only the columns) fits a social relations model to Sampson's monks: like_AB and like_BA binomial with a generalized giving and receiving effect per monk and a correlated dyad pair; its priors were not read. The stack follows kl_dyads: each dyad's two directions become rows, the nominating monk (A, then B) and the nominated one swapping between them. lme4 syntax cannot correlate a monk's giving and receiving effects across the giver and receiver columns, so the two terms are independent here; the dyad pair is (1 | dyad_id) plus the observation-level dyad_id:direction term, exact for a non-negative correlation, and direction enters only that term (ignored). A_name and B_name label A and B; dislike, the second response, is row 2.

ROS Congress (ch. 10 and 15): congress_setup.R builds one row per House district from the 1986, 1988 and 1990 election files in their common district order, with incumbency inc (-1 Republican incumbent, 0 open seat, 1 Democratic incumbent), the Democratic share of the two-party vote v and v_adj, uncontested races set to 0.25 and 0.75. congress.Rmd fits stan_glm(vote ~ past_vote + inc) of the 1988 adjusted share on the 1986 one and predicts 1990, a model of one occasion given the last (published_model no). The long form is district x election year, district numbering the rows, vote named as congress.Rmd names v88_adj and inc as it names inc88. The districts by year are a panel; the proposed model takes the year as a factor and a random intercept per district. v, the unadjusted share, is an alternate response.

formula: MULTDV ~ NCEMP * TIME + TMEXP * TIME + TMPRF * TIME + (TIME | ID)
notes: The help page states the stack and the model: the data 'need to be converted to univariate or stacked form' by make.univ with its defaults, which stack NCPRF.T1 to NCPRF.T3 (newcomer performance at three time points, in order) as MULTDV with TIME 0, 1 and 2 (make.univ's code: rep(0:(NREPOBS - 1))), and Chen's (2005) Table 2 model is lme(MULTDV ~ NCEMP*TIME + TMEXP*TIME + TMPRF*TIME, random = ~TIME|ID, chen2005.univ), filed here. ID (team identifier) is unique per row; TMPRF, TMEXP and NCEMP are team measures taken before the repeated ones and repeat to each occasion. 65 project teams.

GLM-ordinal-regression.myst.md replicates Liddell and Kruschke's IMDB movie ratings: pivot_movie expands each movie's counts n1 to n5 into one rating per rater, coded 0 to 4, with movie and movie_id. The stack keeps the counts, so each long-form row is a movie x rating level, rating the level as the code codes it and n the raters who gave it, a frequency weight (ignored, as twin_hay's freq). The notebook fits movies 1 to 6 only, each by its own OrderedLogistic with Dirichlet-spaced cutpoints and mu ~ Normal(0, 1), against a Normal metric model, so no model pools the movies; the random-intercept cumulative logit over the 36 movies (ID) is a proposal. Descrip is the title.

formula: det ~ date + scale(forest) + scale(ele) + I(scale(ele)^2) + (1 | id)
notes: RULE GAP: two dimensions stacked as one: det991 to det073 (and date991 to date073) are 9 years (1999 to 2007) by 3 visits, survey their column codes (loaded as integers, 991 to 73), and occupancy is closed within a season, so the model needs quadrat x year apart, which no column holds. occupancy.myst.md (after the unmarked vignette, Swiss MHB) fits 2001 only, on the quadrats with all three surveys: a single-season site-occupancy model, z ~ Bernoulli(psi) per quadrat with logit(psi) on scaled forest, scaled ele and its square, and det ~ Bernoulli(z * p) with logit(p) on date (day of year, missing dates imputed by the median). The latent occupancy state has no lme4 form; the formula approximates it by a quadrat random intercept on the detection logit, so confidence is at most medium. surveys counts each quadrat's planned surveys (2 or 3).
